perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He is a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist/colleague there, and they interact professionally and amicably.
- He noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over the past few days.
- He wondered whether he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her, saying she seemed off with him.
- Elizabeth told him no, she was not upset; she said she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He offered to talk and suggested a coffee break.
- Elizabeth accepted the coffee break, thanked him, and said it was kind.
- During coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an outside perspective can sometimes help.
- Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he had not overstepped, and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- Elizabeth said he did not overstep, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break.
- Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot to her, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
